source_text:
㊟: So it should go into futon1b, that's fine.  I know sometimes this makes post-processing (e.g. catch up by 象) ambiguous and my "long turns" look different, but that's a problem to solve in the evidence-processing phase not in the evidence-storage phase (and 象 may remember its rule about triple-greater-than even in the catch-up phase).

㊭ I think we sohuld get back to the idea of thinking about 小象 as a "prior" for 象, and use the corrections of the provisional reading from 象 as a way to train 小象.  We could include a little bit of material about this training process in the writeup at https://hyperreal.enterprises/xiaoxiang.html

㊯ I'd also like you to give me a short draft paragraph that I can send to Brendan Fong that explains how we are working on using his work.  I'm hoping I might be able to arrange a meeting with him to discuss later this week.  (I know we are in a preliminary phase of this work; but maybe it could lead to a joint publication or something later on.)

fragments.text: ㊟: So it should go into futon1b, that's fine.
fragments.target: the agent's proposal to store this in futon1b
fragments.rationale: Draft qualify (1.00), which follows Joe's own ㊟ mark; I relabel to approve. 'it should go into futon1b, that's fine' accepts the agent's storage plan. The qualification comes in the next sentence, where he names a cost of that choice.

fragments.text: I know sometimes this makes post-processing (e.g.
fragments.target: the storage choice: it sometimes makes post-processing ambiguous
fragments.rationale: Accepting the draft's qualify. 'I know sometimes' concedes a cost of putting the turn in futon1b: later processing (such as 象's catch-up) can be unclear.

fragments.text: catch up by 象) ambiguous and my "long turns" look different,
fragments.target: what becomes ambiguous: 象's catch-up reading, and Joe's 'long turns' that look different
fragments.rationale: Accepting the draft's qualify. Completes the concession: the catch-up is ambiguous and his long turns look different from his others.

fragments.text: but that's a problem to solve in the evidence-processing phase not in the evidence-storage phase (and 象 may remember its rule about triple-greater-than even in the catch-up phase).
fragments.target: the ambiguity: it is a problem for the evidence-processing phase, not the evidence-storage phase
fragments.rationale: Draft qualify; I relabel to defer. 'but that's a problem to solve in the evidence-processing phase' sets the ambiguity aside for a later stage and names which stage. The parenthesis adds that 象 may remember its triple->>> rule during catch-up, which is a reason the deferral is safe.

pattern_rejections.reason: Surfaced for deferring to a later stage; read its context/IF/THEN: route a classifier's defers into a typed channel and refine the rule from them. Joe moves an ambiguity to a later phase; no classifier or defer channel is involved.
pattern_rejections.query: keep storage faithful to what was said and solve ambiguity later in the processing phase

fragments.text: ㊭ I think we sohuld get back to the idea of thinking about 小象 as a "prior" for 象, and use the corrections of the provisional reading from 象 as a way to train 小象.
fragments.target: 小象 and 象: treat 小象 as a prior for 象 and train it from 象's corrected provisional readings
fragments.rationale: Accepting the draft's propose. 'I think we should get back to' reopens an idea from earlier: 小象 as a prior for 象, trained by the corrections made to 象's provisional readings. ('sohuld' is a typo.)

pattern_rejections.reason: Read its context/IF/THEN: refine a classifier rule from the cluster shape of its own defers. Close in aim (improve a cheap rule from a record of where it fell short), but the object and the record differ: Joe trains a naive-Bayes prior from corrections to a model's provisional reading.
pattern_rejections.query: a cheap classifier as a prior for a slower annotator, trained on the annotator's corrections

fragments.text: We could include a little bit of material about this training process in the writeup at https://hyperreal.enterprises/xiaoxiang.html
fragments.target: the writeup at hyperreal.enterprises/xiaoxiang.html: add a little material on this training process
fragments.rationale: Accepting the draft's propose. 'We could include' suggests adding a short account of the training to the public writeup.

display_cues.text: include a little bit of material

fragments.text: ㊯ I'd also like you to give me a short draft paragraph that I can send to Brendan Fong that explains how we are working on using his work.
fragments.target: the agent: it is to draft a short paragraph Joe can send to Brendan Fong, explaining how the work uses his
fragments.rationale: Accepting the draft's delegate, which matches Joe's own ㊯ mark. 'I'd also like you to give me' hands the drafting to the agent; Joe will send it himself. The words also fit ask-action.

pattern_rejections.reason: Read its context/IF/THEN: an outward contact with a cold or senior recipient should be deferred until a mission yields a showable artefact. Joe is about to contact Fong and says himself that the work is preliminary; he does not defer, so the pattern's gate does not apply.
pattern_rejections.query: ask for a short draft paragraph to send an outside researcher whose work we are using, to arrange a meeting

fragments.text: I'm hoping I might be able to arrange a meeting with him to discuss later this week.
fragments.target: why the paragraph is wanted: Joe hopes to arrange a meeting with Fong to discuss it later this week
fragments.rationale: Draft delegate; I relabel to explain. Gives the purpose and timing of the draft: a meeting later this week.

fragments.text: (I know we are in a preliminary phase of this work; but maybe it could lead to a joint publication or something later on.)
fragments.target: the paragraph's claims: the work is preliminary, though it might lead to a joint publication
fragments.rationale: Draft delegate; I relabel to qualify. A parenthetical that limits what the draft should promise (preliminary phase) and says what Joe hopes for beyond it.
